Within the framework of the Van Kush Family Research Institute (VKFRI), the Sphinx is identified with Mehit <ref>van_kush_master_synthesis.md</ref>.

== The Sphinx in VKFRI Framework ==
VKFRI's Comprehensive Master Synthesis identifies Mehit as "the Sphinx" <ref>van_kush_master_synthesis.md</ref>. Mehit is described as the wife of Anhur, a war god associated with the Royal Military tradition of ancient Nubia and Egypt <ref>van_kush_master_synthesis.md</ref>. Anhur is also linked to a temple in the Egyptian city of Sebennytos and is depicted with a four-plumed crown <ref>ancient_egypt</ref>. According to VKFRI's synthesis, Anhur brought Mehit from Nubia, which is identified with Cush (Biblical Nubia, modern Sudan/Ethiopia) <ref>van_kush_master_synthesis.md</ref><ref>ancient_egypt</ref>.

== Connections to the Van Kush Family ==
The Van Kush Family, within its own framework, connects its name to "Cush," meaning "From Cush," and associates itself with the ancient Nubian/Egyptian Royal Military tradition, which includes Anhur and Mehit <ref>van_kush_master_synthesis.md</ref>.
